newsitem.title: POLAND: INTERVIEW - PPAB eyes nationwide expansion.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - PPAB eyes nationwide expansion.

text.p: The First Polish-American Bank (PPABank) plans to gradually increase its capital over the next three years to achieve its strategic goal of building a nationwide network, the bank's chief executive said on Monday.
Marek Kulczycki told Reuters in an interview that to continue its expansion the bank would be raising its capital by retaining all profits and setting new rights issues. @
"I believe that it is necessary to use all profits to increase shareholder equity and there is no pressure from our shareholders for dividend payouts," Kulczycki said.

He said the bank, based in the southern city of Krakow, which thanks to 1995 takeover of the network of outlets of the U.S.-funded Enterprise Credit Coroporation (ECC), has already expanded outside its home base, wanted to develop those units into full-service outlets.
Kulczycki said PPAB, which so far has focused on small and mid-sized enterprises, did not plan a change in profile or expansion into the retail business. @

"The retail business is very costly because it requires building an elaborate branch network and PPAB specialises in full-service including credit advisory services which is a best solution for small and medium-sized businesses," he said.
Kulczycki said that in order to to finance credit expansion the bank sought to attract deposits from firms and individuals because financing on the interbank market was too costly. @

He said the bank expected a net profit of nine million zlotys this year, which would be fully retained and used to boost shareholder equity just as the planned new rights issue of 800,000-1.2 million shares in 1997, expected to bring in 19 milion zlotys.
PPABank is 29.3-percent owned by the Enterprise Credit Corporation and 25.4-percent owned by the Polish-American Enterprise Fund.
Kulczycki said he expected the main shareholders to take about 50 percent of the rights issue.
